explain.say: Why would Iceland use volcano heat while Morocco uses the sun? Each country picks the renewable energy that its geography gives it for free. Look at the board: four kinds of renewable energy, each with the places that suit it best.

explain.say: Look at solar first. Deserts get strong sunshine and few clouds, so they are perfect for solar panels and mirrors. Morocco’s Noor power station near Ouarzazate is one of the biggest solar plants in the world, and Rajasthan in India has giant solar parks too. Why do you think clouds matter?

explain.say: Now wind. Windy coasts and open seas suit wind turbines. Denmark is flat and almost surrounded by sea, and gets about half its electricity from wind. Scotland and Gansu in China are windy too. Can you guess why the sea is windier than a city?

faq.q: Why is solar power big in deserts?
faq.a: Deserts have strong sunshine, clear skies and lots of flat, cheap land. That is why huge solar plants are built in places like Morocco, Rajasthan in India and the Atacama in Chile.
asks: Where is solar power used most?
What is the Noor solar plant?

faq.q: Why is Denmark good for wind power?
faq.a: Denmark is flat with a long coastline, and strong, steady winds blow in from the North Sea. It built the world’s first offshore wind farm in 1991.
asks: Where was the first offshore wind farm?

faq.a: Hydroelectric power is electricity made by flowing or falling water spinning turbines, usually at a dam. It needs big rivers and a drop in height, so it suits mountainous, rainy countries.
asks: How does a dam make electricity?

faq.a: Geothermal energy is heat from inside the Earth. Hot water and steam from underground spin turbines or heat homes. It works best near plate boundaries and volcanoes, like in Iceland and Kenya.
asks: How does Iceland use volcano heat?
Why does Iceland use geothermal energy?

faq.a: It depends on the place: sun for deserts, wind for coasts, water for mountains and rivers, heat for volcanic lands. Most countries mix several, because sun and wind change with the weather.
asks: Can a country run only on renewables?

facts: The Three Gorges Dam in China is the world's largest power station by capacity.
Geothermal energy supplies around 45% of Kenya's electricity.
The world's first offshore wind farm, Vindeby, opened in Denmark in 1991.

quiz.say: Which renewable energy suits a sunny desert best?
quiz.show: In a sunny desert, the best renewable energy is…
quiz.why: Deserts have strong sun and few clouds, perfect for solar.

wrong.1: Geothermal needs hot rocks near the surface, found near volcanoes.
wrong.2: Hydro needs big rivers, which deserts rarely have.
